strategy.brief: Position Release Video Engine as a creative-tech product for SaaS founders, developer-tool teams, indie makers and product marketers. The experience should make release automation feel visually desirable, not merely technical: one GitHub release becomes a consistent set of branded launch videos in 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9.
strategy.audience: SaaS founders, developer-tool teams, indie makers, product marketers and creative operators

steps.description: Give us a public GitHub repository and choose the release you want to communicate.

faq.title: Automation should not flatten the creative direction.

items.question: Will every video look the same?
items.answer: No. The template is a reusable brand system, not one universal skin. Product identity, typography, palette, motion intensity and composition rules stay configurable.

items.question: Is this another generic AI video generator?
items.answer: No. The current core is deterministic: structured release data goes through controlled Remotion compositions. AI can assist future workflows, but the visual result is not left to random generation.

items.question: Can I control fonts, colors, logo and motion?
items.answer: Yes. Those are first-class brand inputs. The goal is repeatable creative direction, not a different aesthetic every time you ship.

items.question: Can I use a private repository?
items.answer: The early-access workflow starts with public GitHub repositories so we can validate the product without asking for repository credentials. Private-repository support can follow once the workflow proves demand.

items.question: Who is this actually for?
items.answer: SaaS founders, developer-tool teams, indie makers, product marketers and creative operators who ship frequently but do not want every release to become another manual video-editing task.

contact.title: Bring us your next release.
contact.description: Send a public repository, your work email and how often you ship. We’ll use a real release to show what the workflow can become for your product.

finalCta.title: The next release is already content. Make it look like it.
